title: Coherent cohomology of a projective scheme over a Noetherian ring
statement:
Let $A$ be Noetherian, let $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ be
projective, and let
$\mathcal F$ be a coherent module.
Then $H^q(X,\mathcal F)$ is a finite $A$-module for every $q$.
For an embedding $X\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^n_A$, these groups
vanish for $q>n$.

proof.text: For finiteness, apply finite_H_projective_affine_independent to the specified closed embedding over T=Spec A. Convert its Gamma(T,top)-finiteness to A-finiteness by the identity semilinear map along GammaSpecIso, whose linearity follows from its inverse law.

For vanishing only quasi-coherence is needed: affine pushforward of F along i is quasi-coherent. The projective-space cohomology bound makes H^q(i_*F) subsingleton. The affine-pushforward abelian-cohomology comparison, applied to F as a Cech-acyclic sheaf, injects H^q(F) into this group; hence H^q(F) is subsingleton. This does not require a field or a Noetherian ring.
